es: Narrar una anécdota de 160 a 210 palabras que combine hábito de fondo, giro y reacción con marcadores de secuencia, suspense y una reflexión final.

vocabulary.es: lo siguiente que supe, y de pronto
hacer una pausa para dar efecto

teaching.en: Open with a time marker such as 'In those days' and describe the habit: 'In those days, we would walk to school together and race the ferry.'
teaching.es: Empieza con un marcador temporal como «En aquellos días» y describe el hábito: «En aquellos días, íbamos juntos al colegio y competíamos con el ferry».
teaching.explanationEs: Un marker ordena el tiempo del relato; in those days sitúa un hábito pasado.
segments: Open with a time marker such as 'In those days' and describe the habit:
'In those days, we would walk to school together and race the ferry.'
teaching.audioText: Open with a time marker such as 'In those days' and describe the habit: 'In those days, we would walk to school together and race the ferry.'

teaching.en: Gradually, small things began to change, and the next thing I knew, nobody in the house was speaking at dinner.
teaching.es: Poco a poco, pequeñas cosas empezaron a cambiar y, de pronto, nadie en la casa hablaba durante la cena.
teaching.explanationEs: Gradually marca un cambio lento; the next thing I knew resume un salto brusco.
segments: Gradually, small things began to change, and the next thing
I knew, nobody in the house was speaking at dinner.
teaching.audioText: Gradually, small things began to change, and the next thing I knew, nobody in the house was speaking at dinner.

teaching.en: Meanwhile, my brother was mending the boat, unaware of what was coming, and the contrast between his calm and my unease helps to build up suspense.
teaching.es: Mientras tanto, mi hermano arreglaba el barco, sin saber lo que venía, y el contraste entre su calma y mi inquietud ayuda a acumular suspense.
teaching.explanationEs: Meanwhile une dos acciones simultáneas; va con coma; build up = ir acumulando tensión.
segments: Meanwhile, my brother was mending the boat, unaware of what was coming, and
the contrast between his calm and my unease helps to build up suspense.
teaching.audioText: Meanwhile, my brother was mending the boat, unaware of what was coming, and the contrast between his calm and my unease helps to build up suspense.

teaching.en: To keep the audience in suspense, delay the important detail: 'I opened the door, and then, all of a sudden, I saw...'
teaching.es: Para mantener al público en vilo, retrasa el detalle importante: «Abrí la puerta y entonces, de repente, vi…».
teaching.explanationEs: Los puntos suspensivos y las pausas crean espera; all of a sudden anuncia el giro.
segments: To keep the audience in suspense, delay the important detail: 'I
opened the door, and then, all of a sudden, I saw...'
teaching.audioText: To keep the audience in suspense, delay the important detail: 'I opened the door, and then, all of a sudden, I saw...'

teaching.en: Reveal the twist in one short sentence, preferably after a pause for effect: 'The door was already open.'
teaching.es: Revela el giro en una sola frase corta, preferiblemente tras una pausa para dar efecto: «La puerta ya estaba abierta».
teaching.explanationEs: Reveal = mostrar lo oculto; la frase corta golpea más; pause for effect = silencio buscado.
segments: Reveal the twist in one short sentence, preferably after
a pause for effect: 'The door was already open.'
teaching.audioText: Reveal the twist in one short sentence, preferably after a pause for effect: 'The door was already open.'

teaching.en: Eventually, she told me everything, and little did I know that her story would change the way I saw the whole family.
teaching.es: Al final me lo contó todo, y yo no sabía que su historia cambiaría la forma en que veía a toda la familia.
teaching.explanationEs: Eventually = con el tiempo, al final; no significa «eventualmente». Little did I know anticipa el giro.
segments: Eventually, she told me everything, and little did I know that
her story would change the way I saw the whole family.
teaching.audioText: Eventually, she told me everything, and little did I know that her story would change the way I saw the whole family.

prompt.es: Elige el marcador que mejor abre este hábito del pasado.

choices.text: In those days
All of a sudden
Eventually

feedback.es: «In those days» sitúa un hábito en un tiempo pasado; los otros dos anuncian un cambio brusco o un desenlace.

hint.es: Sitúa el hábito en un tiempo pasado.

origin.text: '___, we would walk to school together every morning and race the ferry across the river.' Which marker fits best at the start of the habit?

prompt.es: Completa: «Retrasó el dato clave para crear suspense antes de la revelación final.»

feedback.es: Suspense es la tensión que se crea al retrasar el dato clave hasta el último momento.

hint.es: Es la tensión de la espera.

origin.text: The writer kept the reader waiting for three paragraphs. By delaying the key detail, she managed to build ___ before the final reveal.

prompt.es: Ordena: «De repente, la calle se quedó en silencio.»

answer.text: All of a sudden the street went quiet

feedback.es: All of a sudden abre la frase y marca el cambio brusco; el resto va en pasado simple.

hint.es: Empieza por el marcador de cambio brusco.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota y elige cómo se revela el final.

choices.text: With a long explanation about why the dog was there.
In one short sentence after a slow, tense build-up.
The narrator never says who was following him.

feedback.es: El miedo crece con marcadores y frases cortas y la revelación llega en una sola frase final: «It was only a dog».

origin.audio: In those days I used to deliver newspapers before school. Gradually the streets became quieter, and every morning I felt as if someone was following me. Meanwhile, my bike light was failing. One dark morning, the next thing I knew, I heard footsteps right behind me. I turned around very slowly. It was only a dog, carrying my missing newspaper in its teeth.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mientras tanto, mi hermana llamaba un taxi sin saberlo.»

feedback.es: Meanwhile une dos acciones que ocurren a la vez y va al principio de la frase con coma.

origin.text: I was packing my bags in the bedroom. ___, my sister was calling a taxi downstairs, unaware that I had changed my mind.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que revela el giro de forma breve y eficaz.

choices.text: After a long time of thinking, I finally understood that the key had been in my own pocket, which surprised me greatly.
Maybe the key was in my pocket, or possibly in a drawer I had not checked yet.
It was in my own pocket.

feedback.es: La revelación funciona mejor en una frase corta y directa; las otras la diluyen con explicaciones o dudas.

origin.text: I spent the whole night searching the house for the missing key. I checked every drawer, every coat and every shoe. At dawn, exhausted, I sat down on the stairs, and only then did I notice where it had been all along.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto crea la narradora con el final del relato.

choices.text: A lasting mystery that the narrator decides not to solve.
A happy ending that solves the mystery of the letter.
A warning about the danger of opening other people's post.

feedback.es: Acaba con una carta para un desconocido y una abuela que sigue mirando a la puerta, sin explicar nada: deja el misterio abierto.

origin.audio: Every evening my grandmother would sit at the window, reading old letters. Gradually she stopped, and the letters gathered dust on the table. One day I found a letter in her basket, still closed. It was addressed to a man I had never heard of, and the date on the envelope was forty years old. I never asked her about it, although I wanted to so badly that I could hardly sleep. But since then, whenever the post arrives, I catch her looking at the door.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué sugiere la última frase de la narradora.

choices.text: That she has completely forgotten who that man was.
That she still hopes for something linked to that letter.
That the post always arrives late in the village.

feedback.es: Que mire a la puerta cada vez que llega el correo sugiere que aún espera algo, aunque la narradora nunca lo diga: es una inferencia.

prompt.es: Completa: «Poco a poco, las estanterías se vaciaron y los clientes dejaron de venir.»

feedback.es: Gradually marca un cambio lento y progresivo, ideal para acumular tensión antes del giro.

origin.text: Nobody noticed the change at once. ___, the shelves emptied and the customers stopped coming, until the shop was silent on a busy street.

prompt.es: Escribe una anécdota de 160 a 210 palabras con hábito, giro y consecuencia.

answer.text: In those days, my grandmother and I would bake bread every Sunday morning. She never used a recipe, and the whole house smelled of warm bread until noon. Gradually, I noticed that she was forgetting the steps, but she laughed it off, and I did not want to ask any questions. Meanwhile, I was busy with school and my friends. One Sunday, she did not come out of her room. I waited in the kitchen, and my hands were cold. Then I saw her sitting on the bed, pale and confused. 'I do not remember the recipe,' she whispered. Eventually, I sat beside her, and we wrote the steps down together. Since that day, I have read the recipe aloud every Sunday. Looking back, I think that quiet morning taught me that love can also mean remembering for someone else.
accepted: In those days, my grandmother and I would bake bread every Sunday morning. She never used a recipe, and the whole house smelled of warm bread until noon. Gradually, I noticed that she was forgetting the steps, but she laughed it off, and I did not want to ask any questions. Meanwhile, I was busy with school and my friends. One Sunday, she did not come out of her room. I waited in the kitchen, and my hands were cold. Then I saw her sitting on the bed, pale and confused. 'I do not remember the recipe,' she whispered. Eventually, I sat beside her, and we wrote the steps down together. Since that day, I have read the recipe aloud every Sunday. Looking back, I think that quiet morning taught me that love can also mean remembering for someone else.

In those days, every Sunday my grandmother and I would make bread together, and she always said that she did not need a book. Little by little, I noticed that she was forgetting the order of the steps. At the same time, I was too busy with my friends to ask her about it. Then, one Sunday, the kitchen was silent. I found her sitting at the table, pale and confused, looking at the flour as if she had never seen it. Finally, I took her hand, and we wrote the recipe on a piece of paper. Since then, I have read it aloud to her every Sunday. Looking back, I realise that I was the one who learned the most that day.

feedback.es: La anécdota combina fondo habitual, marcadores de secuencia, un giro con suspense, la consecuencia y una reflexión final.

origin.text: Datos: cada domingo tu abuela y tú hacían pan; poco a poco notaste que olvidaba los pasos; un domingo no salió de su cuarto; la encontraste sentada y confundida, y te dijo que no recordaba la receta; desde ese día le lees la receta en voz alta cada domingo. Usa marcadores, suspense y una reflexión final.

prompt.es: Lee las dos versiones y elige qué técnica usa la segunda para crear suspense.

choices.text: It describes the key in far more detail than the first version does.
It tells the reader in advance what the box contains.
It builds up the moment and delays the object until the end.

feedback.es: La segunda versión retrasa la aparición del objeto con pausas y detalles, y lo revela al final de la frase: así crea suspense.

origin.text: Version A: 'I opened the box. Inside was a key.' Version B: 'I opened the box slowly. For a moment there was nothing but silence, and then, right at the back, something small and cold caught the light: a key.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la última frase sobre la narradora.

choices.text: That she later saw the decision from her mother's point of view.
That she still blames her mother for selling the old family house.
That she has no memory of the summers by the sea.

feedback.es: «It was years before I understood what it had cost her» indica que con el tiempo entendió a su madre: es la reflexión que cierra el relato.

origin.audio: We used to spend every summer by the sea. Then, all of a sudden, my mother announced that we were selling the house. Eventually we said goodbye to the beach, but I stayed angry for years. It was years before I understood what that decision had cost her.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Yo no sabía que mi vida estaba a punto de cambiar.»

answer.text: Little did I know that my life was about to change

feedback.es: Little did I know va al inicio y anticipa el giro; tras él, el orden normal de la frase.
